look.S46.SARA: Sára keeps a pen next to her computer. When the database fails, the pen doesn’t.
look.S46.ambient 1: Visitor rules. In the biggest letters: no coffee. Not a word about time travel.
look.S46.ambient 2: Every leaf on the ficus points a different way. I’d love to line them up, but I’ll leave it be.
entry.S67.001: Priehyba. This time I’m only changing to another cable car, not to another year.
look.S67.IVAN: Ivan in a down jacket and a woolly hat. Up and down again is an ordinary working day for him. I envy him.
look.S67.ambient 1: First Biela Púť – Priehyba, then the Funitel, Priehyba – Chopok. One change, nothing complicated.
look.S67.ambient 2: A cold handrail. Today I’ve held handrails in five different years, and this is the coldest.
look.S67.boarding: The Funitel to Chopok. Ivan will check my ticket and I can get on.
exit.S67.to_S41.locked: I need a ticket for the cable car. Sára at the customer centre can sort one out for me.
exit.S67.to_S68.locked: First I have to board the Funitel. Ivan will check my ticket.
conn.S67.S68.label: Funitel to Chopok
conn.S67.S68.locked: First I have to board the Funitel. Ivan will check my ticket.
entry.S68.001: At last, a form of transport where everyone travels to the same time.
look.S68.TURISTA: Miloš in a bobble hat. He isn’t noting the altitude; he’s photographing the clouds he likes.
look.S68.ambient 1: Snowy slopes drift slowly by beneath us, dotted with tiny skiers. Nobody’s in a hurry, me included.
look.S68.ambient 2: The Funitel is a different kind of cable car from the gondola below. Wider, and calmer in the wind.
look.S68.arrival: The top station is getting closer. The doors only open once the cabin stops.
exit.S68.to_S47.locked: The doors don’t open during the ride. The top station is already outside the window; I’ll get off there.
exit.S68.to_S67.locked: First I have to board the Funitel. Ivan will check my ticket.
conn.S68.S47.label: Arrival at Chopok
conn.S68.S47.locked: The doors don’t open during the ride. The top station is already outside the window; I’ll get off there.
entry.S47.001: The Rotunda, with the Atlas exhibition inside. The view is beautiful; it’s just that people are vanishing from the photos on the walls.
look.S47.ambient 1: The caption is flawless. The person is missing.
look.S47.ambient 2: An ordinary school bell with an unusually long reach.
look.S47.filter: The panel’s rule: DIFFERENCE = DISCARD. Before editing: a voice, a pause, laughter and two names; after: one dry entry.
look.S47.filter.variant1: The panel now shows the original trace and all the differences. Nothing is discarded automatically.
exit.S47.to_S48.locked: They won’t let me into the pavilion without the service pass from Sára.
exit.S47.to_S68.locked: The doors don’t open during the ride. I’ll get off once we reach the top.
conn.S47.S48.locked: They won’t let me into the pavilion without the service pass from Sára.
entry.S48.001: This equipment belongs to the exhibition. I’m not touching the cable car. I’ll be needing that again.
look.S48.ambient 1: Cables. Even in 2035 there are three too many and one too short.
look.S48.ambient 2: A note saying DON’T SWITCH OFF BLINDLY. NINA. The most important instruction in the room is still handwritten.
look.S48.terminal: I’ll connect the reader here and compare the original and edited records. Nina has allowed diagnostics, not deletion.
exit.S48.to_S47.locked: They won’t let me into the pavilion without the service pass from Sára.
exit.S48.to_S49.locked: The chamber is locked. Only the service terminal can open it.
exit.S48.to_S50.locked: They’ll only let me onto the terrace once the restore procedure is signed.
conn.S48.S49.locked: The chamber is locked. Only the service terminal can open it.
conn.S48.S50.locked: They’ll only let me onto the terrace once the restore procedure is signed.
entry.S45.001: Vrbické pleso under ice. In the middle it’s been swept, and the ice reflects the forest without a single edit.
look.S45.ambient 1: The swept ice reflects the forest and the hill behind it. Slightly crooked, like the horizon on my photo with Gran.
look.S45.ambient 2: A hiking signpost with walking times. In winter only the direction still applies.
look.S45.bench: On the backrest, a ceramic dog and the words DRUHÝ ŽIVOT – ‘second life’. A note underneath: ‘Tamara, during the exhibition, in the lobby of Hotel Grand Jasná.’
look.S45.sensor: A stand from the Atlas exhibition that only measures. I can read it with the chronometer straight from the path.
entry.S50.001: A lovely view. If only Atlas also kept the people looking at it in its records.
look.S50.ambient 1: It would be a shame to simplify those into a triangle.
look.S50.ambient 2: A glass railing, covered in frost. I’ll only lean on it once I’ve put my gloves on.
look.S50.bridge: Atlas’s return connector. A ceramic bridge plugged in here will bypass the faulty write command. The cable cars are separate.
look.S50.switch: WRITE changes the past; MONITOR only reads and allows withheld data to be returned. Without a bridge in the connector, it changes nothing.
look.S50.switch.variant1: The switch is locked in the MONITOR position. Nobody will switch it to WRITE again.
exit.S50.to_S48.locked: They’ll only let me onto the terrace once the restore procedure is signed.
entry.S49.001: We’re high up on Chopok. I’m carrying things from every year I’ve visited today in my bag.
look.S49.VIKTOR: Viktor hasn’t slept, and he badly wants all this to have made sense. He shouldn’t be standing by the big switch alone.
look.S49.ambient 1: Viktor poured it before the start. He hasn’t drunk any yet.
look.S49.ambient 2: The emergency lamp blinks slowly and calmly. No countdown running anywhere.
look.S49.confirm: The restore panel: four ports and a big button. Without MONITOR mode and Viktor’s consent, the restore won’t start.
look.S49.confirm.variant1: The restore is complete. The write-back is switched off, and off it stays.
look.S49.port_consent: The Consent port. The confirmed handover from 2020 goes here.
look.S49.port_origin: The Origin port. The verified imprint from 1962 goes here.
look.S49.port_return: The Return port. The restore procedure from 2035 goes here.
look.S49.port_voice: The Voice port. The original school cassette from 1995 goes here, not a summary of it.
exit.S49.to_S48.locked: The chamber is locked. It only opens once the terminal confirms MONITOR mode.
topic.BORIS.ambient 1.label: Is everything digital?
topic.BORIS.ambient 1.001: Everything has a digital copy. That isn’t the same sentence.
topic.BORIS.ambient 1.x01: A copy tells you what was on the paper. The original also tells you who held it and where their coffee dripped.
topic.BORIS.ambient 1.x02: And the coffee stain isn’t on the copy?
topic.BORIS.ambient 1.x03: It is. But the normaliser cleans it off. And with it, the date that was underneath.
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.label: What if memories differ?
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.001: Two people can remember the same day differently. An archive has to hold both.
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.002: Then someone at Atlas bought shelves that were too narrow.
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.x01: The shelves are fine. What’s narrow is the rule someone stuck on them.
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.x02: And what would you stick on them?
topic.BORIS.ambient 2.x03: Nothing. Shelves get numbers, not opinions.
topic.BORIS.extra 1.label: The oldest exhibit
topic.BORIS.extra 1.001: What’s the oldest thing in the exhibition?
topic.BORIS.extra 1.002: A postcard whose postmark is older than I am. It says the snow is good and the soup is expensive.
topic.BORIS.extra 1.004: It is. Footnote: some news doesn’t change in a hundred years.
topic.BORIS.extra 1.005: Which part? The snow or the soup?
topic.BORIS.extra 1.006: Both. I checked the snow through the window and the soup yesterday in the hotel restaurant.
topic.BORIS.extra 2.label: Sleeve protectors
topic.BORIS.extra 2.001: What are those protectors on your sleeves for?
topic.BORIS.extra 2.002: So that I add nothing to the archive. Not even dust from my own shirt.
topic.BORIS.extra 2.003: And does the archive add anything to you?
topic.BORIS.extra 2.004: All the time. Paper cuts and good stories. In that order.
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.label: Which way now?
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.001: You came up from Biela Púť by gondola; now you take the Funitel to Chopok. Keep your return ticket.
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.002: Today I’m holding on to anything with a return with both hands.
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.x01: Inside pocket is better. It’s windy up there, and tickets fly off like sparrows.
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.x02: Have you had one fly off?
topic.IVAN.ambient 1.x03: Last week, from a gentleman. A piste-basher driver found it two kilometres further down.
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.label: What’s the weather like up top?
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.001: Good today, everything’s running. If that changes, you’ll hear it from me.
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.002: And if it clouds over, what should I go by?
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.x01: By what I tell you. I wouldn’t trust the clouds that much.
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.x02: And how cold is it up there?
topic.IVAN.ambient 2.x03: Minus fourteen and windy – an ordinary February, in other words. Pull your scarf up over your nose.
topic.IVAN.extra 1.label: The Funitel
topic.IVAN.extra 1.001: How is the Funitel different from the gondola below?
topic.IVAN.extra 1.002: It hangs on two cables at once. The wind has a much harder time arguing with it.
topic.IVAN.extra 1.003: And how many people fit in?
topic.IVAN.extra 1.004: A whole ski school, instructor included. And always one more, running to catch up.
topic.IVAN.extra 1.005: There’s one of those in every cabin?
topic.IVAN.extra 1.006: Every one. Usually with one boot undone and one pole.
topic.IVAN.extra 2.label: Working at Priehyba
topic.IVAN.extra 2.001: Doesn’t the same station all day bore you?
topic.IVAN.extra 2.002: The station’s the same; the people are different. Three have already asked me today where Chopok is.
topic.IVAN.extra 2.004: That’s exactly what I told them. Two said thank you, one took offence.
topic.JANA35.ambient 1.001: Maybe. You’ve got the look of someone who’s wandered in here for the second time.
topic.JANA35.ambient 1.002: That guess is more accurate than you’d think.
topic.JANA35.ambient 1.x01: I’m bad with faces. Expressions I remember exactly.
topic.JANA35.ambient 1.x03: Like someone who went to ask the way and fixed something instead.
topic.JANA35.extra 1.label: The exhibition captions
topic.JANA35.extra 1.002: I came to check the captions. An occupational hazard.
topic.JANA35.extra 1.004: Two typos and one ‘approx.’. At an exhibition about memory I’d expect more precision.
topic.JANA35.extra 1.006: I did. He wrote it down and added a footnote underneath: ‘Thank you.’
topic.JANA35.extra 2.label: The school on Sokolíkova
topic.JANA35.extra 2.001: You went to school on Sokolíkova, didn’t you?
topic.JANA35.extra 2.002: Yes. In the same class as Tóno Farkaš. He drew aeroplanes in every exercise book.
topic.JANA35.extra 2.004: Mine too. And I corrected them; the wings were always at the wrong angle.
topic.JANA35.extra 2.006: All except the first. I still have that one in my archive. I don’t touch first versions, even when the wings are crooked.
topic.NINA.ambient 1.label: Is your mother Ela?
topic.NINA.ambient 1.001: Yes. She still writes lists. Only now there’s a holiday on them too.
topic.NINA.ambient 1.002: A holiday? Your mother has a holiday on her list as a task?
topic.NINA.ambient 1.x01: As task number five. After shopping, medicines, phone numbers and the list of lists.
topic.NINA.ambient 1.x03: She ticks it off. Last year she ticked it off in October, in one weekend.
topic.NINA.ambient 2.label: Why Jasná?
topic.NINA.ambient 2.001: For the exhibition we also collect memories of trips. The public part is in the hotel; on Chopok we have a temporary pavilion.
topic.NINA.ambient 2.002: And on the way up, everyone has a reason to look out of the window for a while.
topic.NINA.ambient 2.x01: Exactly. People talk in the gondola. We collected half the exhibition in the queue for the cable car.
topic.NINA.ambient 2.x02: In the queue for the cable car?
topic.NINA.ambient 2.x03: Anyone who stands for twenty minutes with skis on their shoulder will happily tell you how they came here with their dad.
topic.NINA.after.label: What happens to Atlas now?
topic.NINA.after.001: The original records have stayed separate from the edits. And the incident report is public.
topic.NINA.after.x02: He’s writing it himself and hasn’t crossed anything out. That’s new for him.
topic.NINA.after.x04: I’ve added a holiday to my list. Mum will be pleased.
topic.NINA.extra 1.label: The memory of ordinary days
topic.NINA.extra 1.001: What should I imagine under that title?
topic.NINA.extra 1.002: Ordinary days. Shopping lists, postcards, recordings from kitchens.
topic.NINA.extra 1.004: Most of all. They stop for a minute at famous things, and for twenty at a shopping list from 2020.
topic.NINA.extra 1.006: Because everyone is looking to see whether it’s their handwriting.
topic.NINA.extra 2.label: The curator
topic.NINA.extra 2.001: What exactly are you allowed to do as curator?
topic.NINA.extra 2.002: Select, describe and hang. Not delete – nobody is allowed to do that.
topic.NINA.extra 2.004: Not even him. I told him in person, in writing and at the meeting.
topic.NINA.extra 2.006: In person he nodded, in writing he said thank you, and at the meeting he ran the test anyway.
topic.NINA.extra 3.label: Outside all day
topic.NINA.extra 3.001: Aren’t you cold out here? You’ve been standing outside since this morning.
topic.NINA.extra 3.002: I’ve got three layers and a flask from Mum. She still pours my tea, even though I’m thirty.
topic.NINA.extra 3.003: That flask wouldn’t happen to have something written on the side?
topic.NINA.extra 3.004: It does. DO NOT TOP UP WITH SOUP. It’s been on there since 2020.
topic.NINA.extra 3.005: Then that’s the oldest exhibit in the whole exhibition.
topic.NINA.extra 3.006: It’s not an exhibit, it’s a flask. But I’ll tell Mum – she’ll be pleased.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 1.label: How are you doing?
topic.ROBOT.ambient 1.001: Parcels delivered: ninety-nine per cent. Peace of mind: unknown quantity.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 1.x01: Parcels with an address from a human. For example: ‘the entrance where the dog barks’. The dog does not bark all the time.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 1.x02: A human couldn’t find that either.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 1.x03: A human could. A human asks another human. When I ask, people usually tell me I am adorable.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 2.label: Your smile
topic.ROBOT.ambient 2.001: Do those lights mean a smile?
topic.ROBOT.ambient 2.002: They mean the battery is sufficiently charged. An effect on mood is probable.
topic.ROBOT.ambient 2.x01: And when the battery is low?
topic.ROBOT.ambient 2.x02: The lights narrow. People say I am frowning. In winter I frown from four in the afternoon.
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.label: Winter at Biela Púť
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.001: How do you get on driving in this snow?
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.002: Speed: halved. Falls: two this week. Dignity: seventy per cent preserved.
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.003: And who put you back on your wheels?
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.004: A skier and a child. The child drew a smile on my lid at the same time.
topic.ROBOT.extra 1.006: Yes. According to statistics, people help me a third more willingly with it.
topic.ROBOT.extra 2.label: What do you delete?
topic.ROBOT.extra 2.003: Unnecessary But Kind. Contents: three thank-yous, one drawn smile and a song a courier whistled.
topic.ROBOT.extra 2.005: Folder capacity: unlimited. I set it myself.
topic.ROBOT.extra 3.label: The hardest address
topic.ROBOT.extra 3.001: Which address took you longest to find?
topic.ROBOT.extra 3.002: ‘Where the lángos stall used to be.’ Lángos stalls in the area: zero.
topic.ROBOT.extra 3.003: And did you find the place?
topic.ROBOT.extra 3.004: Yes. I asked a lady. She said I was adorable, and then she pointed to exactly where it had been.
topic.SARA.ambient 1.label: Will you sign me in?
topic.SARA.ambient 1.x03: I’ll put today’s. So far, the pen has never once been wrong.
topic.SARA.ambient 2.label: What’s that notebook for?
topic.SARA.ambient 2.001: When names vanish from the system, I write them down here in pen.
topic.SARA.ambient 2.002: And how many names have you got in there today?
topic.SARA.ambient 2.x01: Twenty-three. One gentleman wanted me to write his name with his title.
topic.SARA.ambient 2.x03: I did. When his name vanished from the system, all he had left there was the title.
topic.SARA.extra 1.label: Your pen
topic.SARA.extra 1.001: Do you always write with the same pen?
topic.SARA.extra 1.002: For three years. It’s never fallen on the floor or run out.
topic.SARA.extra 1.004: When I write, I hold it. When I’m not writing, I put it down. And I change the refill on Mondays.
topic.SARA.extra 1.006: I do. Every new colleague, on their first day.
topic.SARA.extra 2.label: What do people ask about?
topic.SARA.extra 2.001: Where the toilets are, when the last gondola goes and whether it’s cold up top.
topic.SARA.extra 2.003: Always. But everyone wants me to say it out loud.
topic.SARA.extra 2.005: I do. And I tell them to zip their jacket right up to the chin.
topic.SARA.extra 3.label: The coffee ban
topic.SARA.extra 3.001: Why is coffee in the biggest letters on the visitor rules?
topic.SARA.extra 3.002: Because once a coffee ended up in the visitors’ book. The names from three pages ran together into one stain.
topic.SARA.extra 3.004: I deciphered them through the stain and rewrote them in pen, one by one. Since then the rule is: coffee outside, pen inside.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.label: Coffee or a repair?
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.001: Coffee is a temporary repair for a person.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.002: And have you got a more permanent repair?
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.x01: And what do people bring you most often?
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.x02: In winter, heated gloves. Only the left one ever heats up, and nobody knows why.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.x03: My guess is a broken wire in the right thumb.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 1.x04: Good guess. You really are a repairer.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.label: Why cassettes?
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.001: With a cassette at least you can see that something is turning.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.002: And with other devices you can’t?
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.x01: You see an indicator light. And that stays on even when everything inside is asleep.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.x02: I know that one. Green, and lying.
topic.TAMARA.ambient 2.x03: That’s the one. A cassette at least admits it’s stopped.
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.label: A workshop in a hotel
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.001: Do you always do your repairs here in the lobby?
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.002: Only during the exhibition. Last year I had my workshop outside by Vrbické pleso, by the bench with the dog.
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.003: And why not now as well?
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.004: In winter my coffee would freeze out there, and the screws.
topic.TAMARA.extra 2.006: Screws don’t, fingers do. And a screw that falls out of them, I won’t find in the snow even with a magnet.
topic.TAMARA.extra 3.label: The promised coffee
topic.TAMARA.extra 3.001: Names have stopped vanishing from your orders. How about that coffee?
topic.TAMARA.extra 3.002: A promise is a promise. Here you are, no sugar.
topic.TAMARA.extra 3.003: How do you know no sugar?
topic.TAMARA.extra 3.004: Repairers haven’t got time to stir.
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.label: Your workshop
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.002: Druhý život – Second Life. Because things have a second life too; people just don’t give it to them.
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.003: And how many lives does a tape recorder like that have?
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.004: As many as the number of times someone repairs it rather than throwing it in the skip.
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.005: I’ve repaired one four times already.
topic.TAMARA.extra 1.006: Then it’s a regular patient. Open a file for it.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.label: Why do you photograph the fog too?
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.001: Because it’s part of the trip too.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.002: I’d like to repeat that sentence to someone up top.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.x01: Go ahead. It’s free, like the fog.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.x02: Today there’s a sea of fog down in the valley and we’re going up above it. The photo will have both.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.x03: And which part do you like better?
topic.TURISTA.ambient 1.x04: The fog. Everybody has clear skies in their photos.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 2.label: Have you been here before?
topic.TURISTA.ambient 2.001: With my father. I don’t remember where we ate. I remember that he laughed.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 2.002: And what did he laugh at?
topic.TURISTA.ambient 2.x01: He laughed because I had my skis on crooked all day.
topic.TURISTA.ambient 2.x03: Today I’d have them on straight. If I hadn’t left them in the car.
topic.TURISTA.extra 1.label: The rucksack
topic.TURISTA.extra 1.001: What do you carry in such a small rucksack?
topic.TURISTA.extra 1.002: I pack like my father did: a flask, schnitzels in foil and spare gloves.
topic.TURISTA.extra 1.004: Everything up there is expensive. A schnitzel only cost me ten minutes at the stove.
topic.TURISTA.extra 1.005: And how many have you got?
